notes: ABIs: arm64-v8a and x86. The rule for an enginehost plugin is arm64-v8a plus x86_64, and x86 is here as the interim answer to it, not as the answer: every x86_64 Android build lists x86 in Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS, so this bundle now runs on an x86_64 device or emulator as a 32-bit library while the 64-bit one is built. What makes x86_64 slower to reach is cocos2d-x 3.17.2, the framework this engine renders and runs on. It does not build nine of the libraries the engine links (z, png, webp, tiff, freetype, chipmunk, BulletCollision, BulletDynamics, LinearMath): each external/<lib>/CMakeLists.txt imports a static library from prebuilt/android/${ANDROID_ABI} (cmake/CocosExternalConfig.cmake:33), and every v3-deps tag of cocos2d-x-3rd-party-libs-bin -- from the v3-deps-158 that cocos2d-x 3.17.2 pins in external/config.json through the last one, v3-deps-172 -- carries armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a and x86 and nothing else. Upstream's own builder for that set defines no x86_64 either (cocos2d-x-3rd-party-libs-src branch v3, build/android.ini: cfg_all_supported_arches=("armv7" "x86" "arm64" "mips")). Those nine are being built from their own sources and staged into that layout; the other seventeen dependencies are a retargeted build, which is what x86 already is.
